doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: Locking in with drummers and the ones you cannot groove with
summary: Smith talks about getting time from the drummer and the players he never felt comfortable with. They joke about Ed Soph's story and about dodging gigs with 'already booked'.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. How about that? I love Masekela’s music. We almost stumbled upon this question that I have on my list here and that was the concept of time between bassists and drummers. Do you have people you’ve played with over the years where you really felt like we are locked in and on the other hand people that you never seem to be able to lock in with? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Yes, on every instrument not just drums, but I’m playing with the drummer when I play, I’m playing with the drummer. I mean that’s where I’m getting my time is with the drummer. And generally the drummer will say I’m getting it with the bass player. So that’s, when you’re both doing that that’s a great thing. And there are — everybody has something good about them. I mean I love playing with different people and there are some people that are very, very successful that I just do not capture a groove with. And I don’t know why but it’s just the way it is. Some people call it chemistry but you know it’s like a thing where you go um hum this isn’t comfortable but you still — on a professional level you’re still playing good time, it just doesn’t feel comfortable or — I hate to even think about it.
Yeah it doesn’t enter into the realm of a train wreck but you’re sort of glad when the gig is over perhaps?
Okay again I did not quite hear the last thing you said.
Well I sometimes — sometimes it’s like, “Oh yeah the gig was okay but I was glad it was over.”

I had an interview recently with a drummer named Ed Soph. And we were talking about this issue. And he said, “I’ve played with bass players and the first tune I go, “Oh God this guy really plays behind the beat so what I do is I go with that bass player and lock up at the slower tempo. The problem is if when I go down to where he is he continues to slow down. That’s a problem.”
Well that problem is easily solved by next time he’s on the gig turn it down. You know what I mean is you may say oh so-and-so is on the gig. “Oh I just realized I’m busy.”
Oh I thought you meant turn the volume down.
No, no, no. No, no. I never fight the drummer, ever. You know it’s definitely a losing game.
Yeah that’s the old, “Oh I wish I could do it but I’m already booked.
Yeah. “Oh man this thing just came up.” Yeah. Yeah.
Do you stall a little bit as if you’re pretending to look at your calendar, right?
Oh look here, “Oh God I didn’t see this, I’m sorry. Man thanks for calling.”
